findings.evidence: Statements at lines 167-172 (`∀ B` outside `∀ᵐ ω` via the `{B}` binder) and 185-191; the file's own docstring at 182-184 says the interchange "is not cosmetic" and is only available for a countable family.
findings.fix: Reword to the delivered order: "for each measurable set, the empirical frequency converges to the directing measure's mass almost surely (and simultaneously for any countable family of sets)."
findings.issue: Module docstring: "Equivalently, the empirical measures converge to the directing measure, setwise and almost surely." Setwise convergence a.s. means ∀ᵐ ω, ∀ B, which is not what any theorem here delivers (each is ∀ B, ∀ᵐ ω) and is false in general: for atomless ν(ω), take B = the countable set of sampled points — empirical mass 1, ν-mass 0, for every ω.

findings.evidence: Line 203: `∀ B : Set α, MeasurableSet B → ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto …` — the null set depends on `B`.
findings.fix: State the actual order in both places: "for every measurable set `B`, almost surely, the empirical mass of `B` converges to `ν ω B`."
findings.issue: Same overclaim in the Main results bullet: `deFinetti_tendsto_empiricalMeasure_apply` is described as giving "a directing measure that is recovered as the almost-sure setwise limit of the empirical measures", and the theorem docstring (lines 193-195) says "recovered, almost surely and on every measurable set" — both read as one null set for all measurable sets.

findings.issue: The facade repeats the overclaim: "the directing measure of an exchangeable process is the almost-sure setwise limit of the empirical measures".

findings.fix: Drop the iff: "the limit reduces to a constant when the directing measure is a.e. constant."
findings.issue: `tendsto_average_ae` docstring claims the limit "reduces to a constant exactly when the directing measure is". The "exactly when" is false in one direction: for `f = 0` (or any `f` whose integral is a.e. constant in `ν ω`) the limit is constant while `ν` is random.

findings.evidence: ConditionallyIID/EmpiricalMeasure.lean:41-49 gives the exact `((n+1)⁻¹ * (…))` identity; lines 65-72 give only `Tendsto … (nhds 0)`.
findings.fix: Cite `ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_empiricalMeasure_apply_sub_sq` for the exact finite-sample error (and keep `tendsto_…_sub_sq` for the convergence).
findings.issue: Cross-reference is wrong: "The mean-square form of the same convergence, with its exact finite-sample error, is `ConditionallyIIDWith.tendsto_integral_empiricalMeasure_apply_sub_sq`" — that lemma only states convergence of the mean-square error to 0; the exact error is a different declaration.

findings.evidence: Line 187: `{B : ι → Set α} (hB : ∀ j, MeasurableSet (B j))`.
findings.fix: Say "from a single measurable set to a countable family of sets under one null set".
findings.issue: Module docstring says what is new includes "the strengthening from a single observable to a whole countable family"; the countable-family result is indexed by measurable *sets*, not observables — no countable-family-of-observables lemma is proved.

summary: Cited declarations and imports check out and every new file and declaration is documented, but the summary prose repeatedly asserts almost-sure *setwise* convergence — the quantifier order the file's own `_ae_forall` docstring says must not be interchanged, and which is false for an atomless directing measure. Two smaller inaccuracies: a false "exactly when" in `tendsto_average_ae` and a cross-reference pointing at the wrong lemma.
